summary.headline: Running is on plan through week 3 (127 of 130 km), but 1:30 looks a long way off and week 4 has started with nothing logged
observations: Weeks 1-3 volume was 41.99, 42.03 and 43.40 km against 42.0, 45.0 and 43.4 planned, about 98% overall. Long runs went 16.0, 17.0 and 18.6 km on schedule.
Run sessions were completed in all three weeks (4, 4 and 5 of the planned runs, plus the intervals in week 3). 11 of 12 were rated as planned; the one exception was the cut-short tempo.
Easy running is controlled and consistent: 5:42-5:50/km at HR 137-140, against a 4-week easy average of 5:47 and 141 bpm.
Quality work is mostly solid. Tempos on Nov 3 (4 km) and Nov 17 (5 km) held 4:36-4:37/km at HR 161-163. The reps on Nov 19 averaged about 4:00/km against 3:55 at HR 171.

The Nov 10 tempo was the exception. Legs were heavy and sleep was poor, the block ran at 5:00/km (slower than the 4:37 target, not faster) with HR 176, and the athlete stopped at 6 km of 9, RPE 8. The next tempo was clean.
Long-run HR is creeping up: 142, 143, then 146 bpm at 5:47, 5:50 and 5:52/km. Efficiency fell from 1.218 to 1.169, and the last run had 186 m of climb.
Strength was 0 of 2 in weeks 1 and 2 and 2 of 2 in week 3 (RPE 7 and 6, 'felt strong'). Only 1 of 3 planned rides was done (46 min on Nov 11).
Week 4 (Nov 23-25) has 0 km logged, so Tuesday's easy 9 km and Strength A are missing. CTL peaked at 49.8 on Nov 22 and has slipped to 46.4 over three days with no load; TSB is -2.6.
No run has an RPE or note, and nothing is logged about the left achilles, so recovery and injury signals are thin.
The goal gap is large. A 44:00 10k (VDOT 46.5) points to roughly 1:36-1:37 for the half, and 4:16/km goal pace is about 21 s/km faster than the 4:37 tempo pace you currently hold at HR 163.
suggestions: If Tuesday's easy run happened, log it. If it was skipped, don't make up the km. Pick up with Thursday's 4 × 0.4 km and the 14.6 km long run on Sunday.
Treat sub-1:30 as the stretch goal and set a realistic target of about 1:35-1:37, then reassess after week 6.
Use the long tempo blocks in weeks 5-7 (2 × 3 km, then 2 × 4 km at 4:37) to check readiness, and consider a short time trial around week 6 to recalibrate paces.
Try to fit in the weekly easy ride and both strength sessions, especially the calf work, since only one ride and two strength sessions are done so far and the achilles is your known weak spot.
Log RPE and a quick note after every run, including any achilles tightness, so the ramp to 44-52 km can be adjusted if needed.
If long-run HR keeps rising at the same pace, or the achilles complains, hold week 7 near 47-48 km instead of 52.
On hard days with poor sleep or heavy legs, swap the session for easy running rather than forcing it, as the Nov 10 tempo showed.
